title: Personal Checking: Paying Items Into Overdraft, Returned Items and Their Fees
content:
## Posting sequence within a business day

On any business day a Personal Checking account books every credit ahead of any debit. Debits are then booked from the smallest amount to the largest; checks of the same amount are booked by ascending check number.

## A debit that would overdraw the account

When a debit would take the ledger balance under zero, the bank's automatic posting process tries an overdraft protection transfer from the linked savings account ahead of any overdraft decision. If no transfer covers the debit, the tier's coverage settings decide what happens:

| Tier offers coverage? | Kind of debit | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| no | ATM withdrawal or debit card transaction | declined; nothing is recorded |
| no | check or ACH debit | returned unpaid and recorded as a returned item, which takes nothing from the balance |
| yes | ATM withdrawal or one-time debit card purchase, owner opted in | paid into overdraft |
| yes | ATM withdrawal or one-time debit card purchase, owner opted out | declined; nothing recorded, no fee |
| yes | check, ACH debit or recurring debit card payment, overdraft no deeper than the coverage limit | paid into overdraft |
| yes | check, ACH debit or recurring debit card payment, overdraft deeper than the coverage limit | returned unpaid |

The debit card overdraft election is read from the account record.

## Fees

- Every item paid into overdraft draws the tier's overdraft item fee, booked as an overdraft item fee entry that names that debit as its source.
- Every returned item draws the tier's returned item fee, booked as a returned item fee entry that names the returned item as its source.
- An item whose amount is at or below the tier's small-item threshold never draws an overdraft fee.
- No overdraft fee and no returned item fee is charged for a business day that ends overdrawn by no more than the tier's end-of-day threshold.
- Overdraft item fees and returned item fees together may not exceed the tier's daily fee count for one account on one business day. They are counted in the order the items posted, and items past the count carry no fee.
- A tier whose fee is 0.00 books no fee entry.
- No single item bears more than one charge of either of these two kinds.
- These fees are charged only while the account status is active. They never attach to credits or to the bank's own fee postings. On a restricted account every debit that would overdraw is returned, and no fee is charged.

Each tier applies its own coverage flag, coverage limit, fees, thresholds and daily count.

## Worked day (hypothetical figures)

An active account with no overdraft link opens a business day at 40.00 USD, on a hypothetical tier with an overdraft item fee of 30.00, a small-item threshold of 3.00, an end-of-day threshold of 60.00 and a daily count of 2. A deposit of 20.00 posts, followed by three checks of 4.00, 70.00 and 90.00 that fit within the coverage limit. The checks post from smallest to largest: 4.00 leaves 56.00; 70.00 leaves negative 14.00, which is an overdraft item; 90.00 leaves negative 104.00, a second overdraft item. The day ends 104.00 below zero, beyond the 60.00 end-of-day threshold, so both overdraft items draw a fee and the daily count of 2 is reached.
